Instead of feeding LLMs 25: disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer 26: needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in 27: verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and 28: Opportunity Scores). 29: 30: This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP 31: communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). 32: 33: We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. 34: 35: ## Code Overview 36: 37: A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) of six 38: installable Python projects plus the React `studio/` front end, each with its own 39: build, tests, and layout: 40: 41: | Package | Description | 42: |---|---| 43: | **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation. | 44: | **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value). | 45: | **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`) | The FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. It talks to the MCP server on the client's behalf and serves the Studio API — configuration, health probes, canvas data, MCP mutations, and streaming (SSE) chat with the LLM tool-loop — plus the built SPA when `studio/dist` exists. | 46: | **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | The local dev **launcher** (`run.py` / `python -m client.run`) that starts the MCP server and the Studio sidecar together. | 47: | **`studio/`** (React + TypeScript + Vite) | **The Living Studio** front end — a spatial, conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation with an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous copilot. Ships as a browser SPA and as a **Tauri 2 desktop app** (`studio/src-tauri/`). | 48: | **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface with an interactive chat mode plus `version`, `update`, `connectors`, and `customer-outcomes` (alias `outcomes`) commands. Data commands are local-first (`--backend local`, default) or remote (`--backend mcp`), with readable tables, `--json`, and a top-level `score`. | 49: | **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`) | Pluggable external integrations. The first kind is an **MCP client connector** that connects to a remote MCP server over HTTP, checks health, and ingests tools/resources into a local ingest sink. Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same protocol later. | 50: 51: ## Quick Start 52: 53: **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package 54: manager. 55: 56: ```bash 57: # Install the entire workspace (all six projects plus dev tooling) 58: uv sync --all-packages 59: 60: # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together 61: npm --prefix studio run build 62: python -m client.run 63: ``` 64: 65: | Service | URL | 66: |---|---| 67: | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | 68: | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | 69: 70: For hot reload, `npm --prefix studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the 71: sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use 72: `npm --prefix studio run tauri dev`. See 73: [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). 74: 75: The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support to drive its 76: agent — see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md). 77: 78: ### CLI at a glance 79: 80: The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: 81: 82: ```bash 83: python -m cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version 84: python -m cli --help # show available options and commands 85: python -m cli # start interactive chat in a terminal 86: agentic-odi customer-outcomes list 87: agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 88: ``` 89: 90: Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server 91: (`python -m mcp_server`). 23: ## The Rule
24: 
25: **Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

32:

1: # Repository Architecture
2: 
3: Agentic ODI is a uv workspace with a single root `pyproject.toml` for shared tooling. Python distributions are imported by their stable `agentic_odi_*` package names; directory layout does not leak into imports.
4: 
5: ## Layout
6: 
7: ```text
8: apps/
9:   cli/            agentic_odi_cli         Typer CLI: local SQLite or remote MCP
10:   mcp-server/     agentic_odi_mcp_server  FastMCP server over HTTP
11:   studio-api/     agentic_odi_studio_api  FastAPI sidecar for the Studio SPA
12:   studio/         React + TypeScript + Vite SPA and Tauri 2 shell
13: packages/
14:   core/           agentic_odi_core        Domain, services, repositories, contract
15:   connectors/     agentic_odi_connectors  MCP client connectors and catalog
16: infra/cloudflare/ Worker + Wrangler config for the free-plan deployment
17: scripts/          Dev launcher, binary build, installer checks
18: tests/            Cross-package contract and launcher tests only
19: docs/             Architecture, reference material, Superpowers artifacts
20: packaging/        PyInstaller spec for the CLI binary
21: ```
22: 
23: ## Dependency Direction
24: 
25: ```text
26: apps/cli ──────────────┐
27: apps/mcp-server ───────┼──▶ packages/core
28: apps/studio-api ───────┘         ▲
29:                                  │
30: apps/cli ──────────────▶ packages/connectors
31: ```
32: 
33: - `packages/core` depends on no other workspace package.
34: - `packages/connectors` depends on `core` only where it needs shared models.
35: - Every runnable app may depend on `core`; none of them imports another app.
36: - The React SPA only talks to `apps/studio-api` over `/api`; it never calls MCP or the LLM directly.
37: 
38: ## Persistence
39: 
40: - `SQLiteRepository` is the production default for the CLI, MCP server, and Studio API.
41: - The default database is `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`.
42: - `build_repository()` chooses SQLite by default and `InMemoryRepository` when `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:`, which is what tests use.
43: - The CLI selects its backend with `--backend local|mcp` or `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND`.
44: - The Studio API selects `local` (direct service calls) or `mcp` (passthrough) with `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` or `create_app(backend=...)`.
45: 
46: ## MCP Contract
47: 
48: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` owns `ToolName`, `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_SPECS`, and `TOOL_NAMES`. The live FastMCP registry is asserted against it by `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py`; the CLI's local handlers are checked by `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py`.
49: 
50: ## Entry Points
51: 
52: | Command | Module |
53: |---|---|
54: | `agentic-odi` | `agentic_odi_cli.cli:app` |
55: | `agentic-odi-server` / `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | `agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server:main` |

1: # Data Flow
2: 
3: ## Sources of Truth
4: 
5: | Layer | Owns | Persists |
6: |---|---|---|
7: | `packages/core` | `Job`, `Step`, `Outcome`, `CustomerOutcome`, `ODIService`, repository protocol | SQLite event log + snapshots |
8: | `apps/mcp-server` | MCP tool adapters over `ODIService` | `build_repository()` selects SQLite in production and in-memory for `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` |
9: | `apps/studio-api` | Studio API, canvas projection, chat tool loop | Via the same repository when the local backend is active |
10: | `apps/studio` | Presentation state, optimistic canvas updates | Browser cache only |
11: | `apps/cli` | Terminal rendering, local/remote backend selection | SQLite directly for `local`, no local writes for `mcp` |
12: 
13: ## Write Paths
14: 
15: ### Local CLI
16: 
17: ```text
18: agentic-odi customer-outcomes add
19:   -> LocalBackend
20:   -> ODIService
21:   -> SQLiteRepository
22:   -> IntentStore (append) + snapshot refresh
23: ```
24: 
25: ### MCP
26: 
27: ```text
28: MCP client / Studio MCP mode / CLI --backend mcp
29:   -> FastMCP tool
30:   -> ODIService
31:   -> configured Repository
32: ```
33: 
34: `apps/mcp-server` builds its repository once at import time with `build_repository()`. Production uses SQLite; tests set `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` (the root test suite does this in `tests/conftest.py`).
35: 
36: ### Studio API
37: 
38: ```text
39: apps/studio SPA
40:   -> /api/canvas, /api/steps, /api/outcomes
41:   -> backend=local: ODIService -> Repository
42:   -> backend=mcp:   call_mcp_tool -> MCP server -> ODIService -> Repository
43: 
44: apps/studio SPA
45:   -> /api/chat
46:   -> stream_chat -> OpenAI-compatible LLM -> MCP tool calls
47: ```
48: 
49: The SPA sends `mcp_url` with every data request for compatibility. In `local` mode the sidecar ignores it; in `mcp` mode it is required for canvas and mutations.
50: 
51: ## Read Paths
52: 
53: ```text
54: ODIService.get_jobs / get_job_map / get_outcomes
55:   -> Repository read-through state
56:   -> Pydantic models
57:   -> JSON (CLI --json, MCP text payload, Studio canvas)
58: ```
59: 
60: The Studio canvas falls back to the demo seed only in `mcp` mode when MCP is unreachable or returns no jobs. `local` mode returns exactly what is in the local database, including an empty canvas.
61: 
62: ## Configuration
63: 
64: | Variable | Used by | Default |
65: |---|---|---|
66: | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | core SQLite repository | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` |
67: | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | CLI, Studio API | `local` |
68: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | CLI, Studio defaults | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
69: | `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST` | Studio API, dev launcher | `apps/studio/dist` |
70: | `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT` | Tauri shell | auto-detected |
71: | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
72: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local-tools-model` |
73: | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local` |
74: 
75: ## Trust Boundaries
76: 
77: - The SPA runs in a browser or Tauri webview and only trusts the sidecar origin.
78: - The sidecar may reach MCP and the LLM; CORS is restricted to known Studio origins.
79: - MCP is an HTTP service with no authentication in local development. Do not expose it directly to the internet; the Cloudflare setup tunnels the sidecar, not MCP.

(End of file - total 79 lines)

1: # Testing
2: 
3: ## Commands
4: 
5: ```bash
6: uv run pytest                       # all packages + root contract/launcher tests
7: uv run pytest packages/core         # one package
8: uv run pytest tests/contract        # MCP contract only
9: uv run mypy apps packages tests
10: uv run ruff check .
11: uv run ruff format --check .
12: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages
13: ```
14: 
15: The root `pyproject.toml` owns pytest, coverage, ruff, mypy, and bandit configuration. There is no per-package test configuration to keep in sync.
16: 
17: ## Layout
18: 
19: Tests live next to their package (`packages/*/tests`, `apps/*/tests`). Root `tests/` contains only cross-package checks:
20: 
21: - `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` — live FastMCP names, argument names, and required fields match `agentic_odi_core.contract.TOOL_SPECS`.
22: - `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py` — the CLI local-handler keys are a subset of `TOOL_NAMES`.
23: - `tests/scripts/` — dev launcher helpers and lifecycle.
24: 
25: ## Isolation Rules
26: 
27: - Use `InMemoryRepository` in tests. `create_app(InMemoryRepository())` keeps the Studio API off the real `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`.
28: - The MCP server uses `build_repository()`; tests set `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` before import and call tools through `Client(mcp)` without HTTP.
29: - Async tests use `@pytest.mark.asyncio` (strict mode).
30: 
31: ## Coverage
32: 
33: CI runs the root suite on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12, collects coverage for every `agentic_odi_*` distribution, and uploads `coverage.xml` from the 3.12 job. Codecov requires 90% project coverage; patch coverage is advisory. Python tests and `apps/studio/**` are excluded from the report by `codecov.yml`.
34: 
35: ## Frontend
36:

38: npm --prefix apps/studio run lint
39: npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck
40: npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run
41: npm --prefix apps/studio run build
42: cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
43: ```

1: # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails
2: 
3: This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.
4: 
5: > **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `knowledge/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails
10: 
11: This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.
12: 
13: ### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?
14: 
15: ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.
16: 
17: ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done
22: 
23: - A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
24: - A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
25: - **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
26: - ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes
31: 
32: - **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
33: - Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
34: - **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):
35: 
36:   > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`
37: 
38:   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
39:   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
40:   - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
41:   - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.
42: 
43: - **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)
48: 
49: - All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
50:   1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
51:   2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
52:   3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
53:   4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
54:   5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
55:   6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
56:   7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
57:   8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs
58: 
59: - **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
60: - ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)
65: 
66: - Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
67:   - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
68:   - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?
69: 
70: - **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):
71: 
72:   ```
73:   Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
74:   ```
75: 
76: - **Interpretation**:
77:   - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
78:   - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
79:   - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.
80: 
81: - **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation
86: 
87: - ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
88: - Segments can be:
89:   - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
90:   - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
91:   - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value
92: 
93: - **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy
98: 
99: Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:
100: 
101: | Strategy | When to use |
102: |---|---|
103: | **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
104: | **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
105: | **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |
106: 
107: - **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: ### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent
112: 
113: These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:
114: 
115: | DO | DON'T |
116: |---|---|
117: | Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
118: | Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
119: | Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
120: | Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
121: | Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
122: | Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
123: | Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## 🛠 Technology Stack & Tools
128: - **Language**: Python 3.10+
129: - **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)
130: - **ASGI Server**: `uvicorn`
131: - **HTTP Client**: `httpx`
132: - **UI / Chat Client**: `streamlit`
133: - **LLM Client**: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible, used with Ollama locally)
134: - **Concurrency**: `asyncio`
135: - **Data Modeling / Validation**: `pydantic`
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## 📄 README Maintenance Guardrail
140: 
141: `README.md` is the **primary human-facing entry point** for this project: a short,
142: high-level front door aimed at both users and developers. Detailed material lives
143: in `docs/` and is linked from the README. The agent MUST keep both current at all
144: times.
145: 
146: ### When to update
147: 
148: Update the relevant file whenever any of the following change:
149: 
150: | Change type | Where to update |
151: |---|---|
152: | New or removed Python file / package | `README.md` **Code Overview** |

162: 
163: ### Rules
164: 
165: - ✅ **Update docs in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
166: - ✅ **Keep README short**: it stays a high-level orientation page. Push detail into `docs/` and link to it rather than growing the README.
167: - ✅ **Keep the Quick Start accurate**: always reflect `python -m client.run` as the recommended launch command.
168: - ✅ **Keep Prerequisites up to date**: add any new `pip install` dependency immediately.
169: - ✅ **Mark Roadmap items `[x]` when completed** — do not leave stale unchecked items.
170: - ❌ **Never leave the README or `docs/` in a stale state** where documented commands or files no longer match the codebase.
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: ## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails
175: 
176: ### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
177: - **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
178: - **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
179:   - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
180:   - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
181: - **Tool Creation**: 
182:   - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
183:   - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
184:   - **Capability Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `mcp_server/src/mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update the `get_capabilities` tool's human-readable return string to ensure the capability set exactly matches the code.
185: 
186: ### 2. Async / Client Practices
187: - Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
188: - Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.
189: 
190: ### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
191: - Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
192: - When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.
193: 
194: ### 4. General Philosophy
195: - **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
196: - **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
197: - **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `connectors/` workspace package. New kinds implement `connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
198: - **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.
199: 
200: ### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
201: - **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
202: - **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
203: - **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `mcp_server/src/mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `connectors/src/connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
204: - **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
205: - **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
206: - **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
207: - **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.

51: ## Formatting workflow

66: ## Pre-commit hooks

90: uv run --directory local_server pytest

96: ## Test Coverage
97: 
98: CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12**, combines each package's
99: coverage into one `coverage.xml`, and uploads it to
100: [Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) from the 3.12 job. Each
101: matrix job also stores its combined report as a build artifact.
102: 
103: The Codecov upload authenticates with the `CODECOV_TOKEN` repository secret and
104: is non-blocking (`fail_ci_if_error: false`), so a Codecov outage or a fork PR
105: without secrets cannot fail the test job. The badge at the top of the README
106: tracks `main`, which is the baseline every PR is compared against:

1: # CLI Reference
2: 
3: The `agentic-odi` CLI is a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based
4: command-line interface for working with Agentic ODI without a chat UI. It
5: provides an interactive chat mode plus version, update, and data commands. Data
6: commands are **local-first**: they read and write a SQLite store with no server
7: required, and switch to a remote MCP server with `--backend mcp`.
8: 
9: Install the workspace first if you have not already:
10: 
11: ```bash
12: uv sync --all-packages
13: ```
14: 
15: ## Launching
16: 
17: ```bash
18: python -m cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
19: python -m cli --help      # show available options and commands
20: python -m cli             # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped)
21: ```
22: 
23: A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.
24: 
25: ## Global options
26: 
27: | Option | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
28: |---|---|---|---|
29: | `--backend local\|mcp` | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | `local` | Run in-process against SQLite, or call a remote MCP server. |
30: | `--db PATH` | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` | Store path for the `local` backend. |
31: | `--mcp-url URL` | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | Server URL for the `mcp` backend. |
32: 
33: Data commands print readable tables and blocks by default; add `--json` for
34: machine-readable output. Diagnostics go to stderr and failures exit non-zero
35: (`0` success, `1` error, `2` usage error).
36: 
37: ## Interactive chat
38: 
39: `agentic-odi chat` (or simply `agentic-odi` in a terminal) starts a
40: conversational session against the MCP server and an OpenAI-compatible LLM.
41: Responses stream to the terminal, and the assistant can call the ODI MCP tools
42: as it talks.
43: 
44: ```bash
45: agentic-odi chat
46: agentic-odi chat --model local-tools-model --mcp-url http://localhost:8000/mcp
47: ```
48: 
49: Before starting, run the MCP server (`python -m mcp_server`) and point the chat
50: at an OpenAI-compatible model endpoint. The chat reads the same environment
51: variables as the Living Studio:
52: 
53: | Variable | Default | CLI flag |
54: |---|---|---|
55: | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | `--base-url` |
56: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | `--model` |
57: | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | `--api-key` |
58: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | `--mcp-url` |
59: 
60: Inside the session, `/help` lists the commands, `/tools` lists the MCP tools the
61: assistant can call, `/clear` resets the conversation, and `/exit` (or `/quit`)
62: ends the session.
63: 
64: > [!NOTE]
65: > Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The `customer-outcomes`
66: > and `connectors` commands keep working without one.
67: 
68: ## Manage Customer Outcomes
69: 
70: Customer Outcomes link customer value to business value. The `local` backend
71: writes to the shared SQLite store with no server required; add `--backend mcp`
72: to route through a running MCP server (`python -m mcp_server`). The group is also
73: available under its historical name `outcomes`.
74: 
75: ```bash
76: # Add a Customer Outcome
77: agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
78:   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
79:   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
80:   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 \
81:   --category cost_reduction \
82:   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"
83: 
84: # List outcomes (optionally filtered, or as JSON)
85: agentic-odi customer-outcomes list
86: agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
87: agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --json
88: 
89: # Get, update, delete
90: agentic-odi customer-outcomes get <outcome-id>
91: agentic-odi customer-outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
92: agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
93: 
94: # Compute an ODI Opportunity Score (top-level, also under the group)
95: agentic-odi score 8 2
96: agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
97: ```
98: 
99: `score` applies the ODI opportunity formula,
100: `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`.
101: 
102: Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (or `--mcp-url`) to point to a non-default server when
103: using `--backend mcp` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
104: 
105: ## Connectors
106: 
107: The `connectors` group manages external MCP integrations. See
108: [External Connectors](connectors.md) for presets, the connector registry, and
109: ingest behavior.
110: 
111: ```bash
112: python -m cli connectors catalog
113: python -m cli connectors add mcp --preset github
114: python -m cli connectors list
115: python -m cli connectors health --name github
116: python -m cli connectors ingest --name github
117: ```
118: 
119: ## Updates
120: 
121: `odi update` checks for and installs a new binary release. Auto-update is on by
122: default; disable it with `--no-update` for one run or
123: `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1` globally. See [Installation](installation.md).

2: 
3: Connectors are named integrations stored in `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (or a
4: path you pass with `--config` / `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE`). The first kind is
5: `mcp`: Agentic ODI acts as an MCP **client** and pulls catalog, resources, and
6: optional tool results from an external MCP **server**.
7: 
8: ## Presets
9: 
10: The fastest way to connect is a preset. `connectors catalog` lists every
11: built-in preset, grouped by the capability area it serves:
12: 
13: ```bash
14: python -m cli connectors catalog                          # all presets
15: python -m cli connectors catalog --area strategy-alignment
16: python -m cli connectors catalog --json
17: ```
18: 
19: | Capability area (`--area`) | Presets |
20: |---|---|
21: | Voice of customer & qualitative research (`voice-of-customer`) | `notion`, `gong`, `fireflies`, `intercom`, `confluence` |
22: | Quantitative data & opportunity scoring (`quantitative-data`) | `posthog`, `amplitude`, `mixpanel` |
23: | Market & competitive intelligence (`market-intelligence`) | `exa`, `tavily` |
24: | Product strategy & backlog alignment (`strategy-alignment`) | `linear`, `github`, `jira`, `miro`, `figma` |
25: | Strategy & knowledge management output (`knowledge-output`) | `slack` |
26: 
27: Register one with `--preset`; `--name` defaults to the preset id:
28: 
29: ```bash
30: # Token-based preset: export the variable it needs first
31: export GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=ghp_...
32: python -m cli connectors add mcp --preset github
33: python -m cli connectors health --name github
34: python -m cli connectors ingest --name github
35: 
36: # OAuth-based preset: the browser consent flow starts on first use
37: python -m cli connectors add mcp --preset notion
38: ```
39: 
40: Credentials never enter the registry. Presets that use API keys store `${VAR}`
41: placeholders that are resolved from the environment when a connection is
42: opened, and `connectors health` names any variable that is missing. `--url`
43: overrides the endpoint (self-hosted or proxied deployments) and `--tool` still
44: selects which tools to call during ingest.
45: 
46: Custom servers keep working the same way:
47: 
48: ```bash
49: python -m cli connectors add mcp --name internal --url https://mcp.internal.example/mcp --tool latest_quote
50: python -m cli connectors list
51: ```
52: 
53: > [!NOTE]
54: > Presets cover MCP servers with a hosted endpoint. Servers you run yourself
55: > (Snowflake, BigQuery, Google Drive, Brave Search, and similar) are added with
56: > an explicit `--url`. The catalog lives in
57: > `connectors/src/connectors/catalog.py`.
58: 
59: > [!NOTE]
60: > OAuth tokens are cached in memory for the life of one CLI process, so an OAuth
61: > preset may ask for consent again on the next `connectors health` or
62: > `connectors ingest`. Prefer a token-based preset where the server offers one.
63: 
64: ## Ingest behavior
65: 
66: Ingested records are normalized (`catalog`, `resource`, `tool_result`) and
67: appended to the in-process ingest sink. They are **not** written into the ODI
68: jobs/outcomes store — mapping ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts is still on
69: the [roadmap](roadmap.md).
70: 
71: Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same
72: `Connector` protocol later.

1: # Running The Living Studio
2: 
3: **The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
4: an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
5: Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
6: connected to the MCP server.
7: 
8: The Studio runs three ways. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to
9: the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM
10: directly.
11: 
12: ## Architecture
13: 
14: ```text
15: ┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
16: │  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  local_server (sidecar)       │
17: │  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
18: │  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
19: └────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
20:                                              │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
21:                                              └───────────────┬───────────────┘
22:                                                              │ MCP (HTTP)
23:                                                              ▼
24:                                              ┌───────────────────────────────┐
25:                                              │  mcp_server  :8000/mcp        │
26:                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
27:                                                              ▲
28:                                                              │ OpenAI-compatible
29:                                              ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
30:                                              │  Your local LLM backend       │
31:                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
32: ```
33: 
34: ## 1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)
35: 
36: ```bash
37: npm --prefix studio run build   # build the SPA into studio/dist
38: python -m client.run            # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100
39: ```
40: 
41: | Service | URL |
42: |---|---|
43: | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
44: | Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 |
45: 
46: `python -m client.run` starts both processes concurrently; press **Ctrl+C** to
47: stop both.
48: 
49: ## 2. Web — dev with hot reload
50: 
51: Vite proxies `/api` to the sidecar:
52: 
53: ```bash
54: npm --prefix studio run dev:full   # MCP + sidecar + Vite together
55: # open http://localhost:5173
56: ```
57: 
58: ## 3. Desktop — Tauri 2
59: 
60: The app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself:
61: 
62: ```bash
63: npm --prefix studio run tauri dev     # dev window
64: npm --prefix studio run tauri build   # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows)
65: ```
66: 
67: > [!NOTE]
68: > **Tauri prerequisites.** The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and
69: > Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu:
70: >
71: > ```bash
72: > sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \
73: >   libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64
74: > ```
75: >
76: > The Tauri CLI ships as the `@tauri-apps/cli` npm dev dependency
77: > (`npm --prefix studio run tauri`). The sidecar is launched with
78: > `uv run python -m …` from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the
79: > repo root, set `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT`.
80: 
81: ## Desktop signing & updater secrets
82: 
83: Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an
84: unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub
85: Actions secrets.
86: 
87: | Secret | Purpose |
88: |---|---|
89: | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate`. |
90: | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). |
91: | `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. |
92: | `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. |
93: | `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. |
94: | `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. |
95: 
96: Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag
97: is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via
98: **Settings → Check for updates**.
99: 
100: ### Managing the updater signing key
101: 
102: The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can
103: verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is
104: embedded in `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is
105: safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in
106: CI, or attached to a build artifact.
107: 
108: 1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a
109:    passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:
110: 
111:    ```bash
112:    npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f
113:    ```
114: 
115:    This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub`
116:    (public).
117: 
118: 2. **Paste the public key** into `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`:
119: 
120:    ```jsonc
121:    {
122:      "plugins": {
123:        "updater": {
124:          "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
125:          "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
126:        }
127:      }
128:    }
129:    ```
130: 
131: 3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is
132:    git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:
133: 
134:    ```bash
135:    mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
136:    mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
137:    chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
138:    ```
139: 
140:    Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/
141:    Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives.
142:    Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing
143:    installs.
144: 
145: 4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and
146:    variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:
147: 
148:    ```bash
149:    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
150:    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password
151:    ```
152: 
153: 5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed):
154: 
155:    ```bash
156:    gh secret list
157:    ```
158: 
159: 6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the
160:    new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into
161:    their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public
162:    key ahead of the cut-over.
163: 
164: > [!CAUTION]
165: > If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new
166: > pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.
167: 
168: > [!IMPORTANT]
169: > **Migration note.** The Streamlit UI (`client/src/client/app.py`) has been
170: > removed. The Living Studio now lives in `studio/` (browser SPA + Tauri desktop
171: > app) and is served by the `local_server` sidecar on port **8100** (previously
172: > Streamlit's `8501`). Start everything with `python -m client.run`. All
173: > `AGENTIC_ODI_*` environment variable names, the demo dataset, and the ODI
174: > formulas are unchanged.
175: 
176: ## Connecting an LLM
177: 
178: The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM backend with tool-calling support to
179: drive the agent. For a fully local setup, see
180: [Local LLM Backend](local-llm.md).
181: 
182: ## Agent-Driven Testing
183: 
184: Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it starts
185: both processes, opens the browser, sends a test message, and reports the results.
186: 
187: Type `/test` to have the agent run all tests and report the results
188: automatically.

(End of file - total 188 lines)
</content>

1: """
2: Local dev launcher for Agentic ODI.
3: 
4: Starts the FastMCP server (``python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server``) and the Living
5: Studio sidecar (``uvicorn agentic_odi_studio_api.app:create_app --factory``)
6: concurrently, then prints the MCP and Studio URLs. Shutting down this script
7: (Ctrl+C) terminates both processes.
8: 
9: Usage:
10:     uv run python scripts/dev.py
11: """
12: 
13: from __future__ import annotations
14: 
15: import os
16: import signal
17: import socket
18: import subprocess  # nosec B404 - launches only fixed child commands (see B603 notes)
19: import sys
20: import time
21: 
22: MCP_PORT = 8000
23: STUDIO_PORT = 8100
24: 
25: REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
26: SPA_DIST = os.environ.get(
27:     "AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST", os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "apps", "studio", "dist")
28: )
29: SPA_BUILD_HINT = (
30:     "Frontend not built — run `npm --prefix apps/studio run build` to serve the Studio UI."
31: )
32: 
33: 
34: def is_port_in_use(port: int) -> bool:
35:     with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
36:         return s.connect_ex(("localhost", port)) == 0
37: 
38: 
39: def build_commands() -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
40:     """Return the (mcp_server, sidecar) argv lists, both shell-free and fixed."""
41:     mcp_command = [sys.executable, "-m", "agentic_odi_mcp_server"]
42:     sidecar_command = [
43:         sys.executable,
44:         "-m",
45:         "uvicorn",
46:         "agentic_odi_studio_api.app:create_app",
47:         "--factory",
48:         "--host",
49:         "127.0.0.1",
50:         "--port",
51:         str(STUDIO_PORT),
52:     ]
53:     return mcp_command, sidecar_command
54: 
55: 
56: def start_server() -> subprocess.Popen:
57:     if is_port_in_use(MCP_PORT):
58:         print(f"Error: Port {MCP_PORT} is already in use.")
59:         print("Please stop any process running on this port and try again.")
60:         sys.exit(1)
61: 
62:     mcp_command, _ = build_commands()
63:     print(f"Starting MCP server on http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}/mcp ...")
64:     # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
65:     return subprocess.Popen(mcp_command)  # nosec B603
66: 
67: 
68: def start_studio() -> subprocess.Popen:
69:     if is_port_in_use(STUDIO_PORT):
70:         print(f"Warning: Port {STUDIO_PORT} is already in use. The sidecar may fail to start.")
71: 
72:     _, sidecar_command = build_commands()
73:     print(f"Starting Living Studio sidecar on http://localhost:{STUDIO_PORT} ...")
74:     # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
75:     return subprocess.Popen(sidecar_command)  # nosec B603
76: 
77: 
78: def main() -> None:
79:     server = None
80:     studio = None
81: 
82:     def shutdown(signum=None, frame=None):
83:         print("\nShutting down...")
84:         if studio:
85:             studio.terminate()
86:         if server:
87:             server.terminate()
88: 
89:         try:
90:             if studio:
91:                 studio.wait(timeout=5)
92:             if server:
93:                 server.wait(timeout=5)
94:         except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
95:             if studio:
96:                 studio.kill()
97:             if server:
98:                 server.kill()
99: 
100:         print("✅ All processes stopped.")
101:         sys.exit(0)
102: 
103:     signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, shutdown)
104:     signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, shutdown)
105: 
106:     try:
107:         server = start_server()
108:         # Give the server a moment to bind its port before the sidecar connects
109:         time.sleep(2)
110:         studio = start_studio()
111: 
112:         print("\nBoth processes are running.")
113:         print(f"MCP Server   -> http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}/mcp")
114:         print(f"Living Studio -> http://localhost:{STUDIO_PORT}")
115:         if not os.path.isdir(SPA_DIST):
116:             print(f"\n⚠️  {SPA_BUILD_HINT}")
117:         print("\nPress Ctrl+C to stop both.\n")
118: 
119:         # Wait for either process to exit unexpectedly
120:         while True:
121:             rc_server = server.poll()
122:             rc_studio = studio.poll()
123: 
124:             if rc_server is not None:
125:                 print(f"\nServer exited unexpectedly (code {rc_server}).")
126:                 break
127: 
128:             if rc_studio is not None:
129:                 print(f"\nStudio sidecar exited unexpectedly (code {rc_studio}).")
130:                 break
131: 
132:             time.sleep(1)
133: 
134:     except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
135:         print(f"\nError: {e}")
136:     finally:
137:         shutdown()
138: 
139: 
140: if __name__ == "__main__":
141:     main()

172:     if target is None:

177:             return

183:             update.perform_update(target, archive, digest, paths.install_root())
184:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001

186:         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from exc

1: # Installation
2: 
3: Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Install the latest
4: release with one command:
5: 
6: ```bash
7: curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
8: ```
9: 
10: The installer places the binary under `~/.local/share/agentic-odi/versions/<version>/`,
11: creates a `current` symlink, and symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and
12: `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`.
13: 
14: If `~/.local/bin` is not on your PATH, add it (e.g.,
15: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`). On Windows, the PowerShell installer
16: uses `~\AppData\Local\agentic-odi\` and copies `.exe` files to
17: `~\AppData\Local\agentic-odi\bin\`.
18: 
19: ## Update
20: 
21: By default, `odi` auto-checks for updates once every 24 hours and applies the
22: update on the next run (auto-update is enabled by default). Control behavior
23: with:
24: 
25: - `odi update` — explicit check and update
26: - `--no-update` flag — skip auto-update for this run
27: - `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1` — disable auto-update globally
28: 
29: When running from a non-frozen source install, auto-update is suppressed
30: automatically.
31: 
32: ## Install layout
33: 
34: ```text
35: ~/.local/share/agentic-odi/
36:   ├── versions/<version>/
37:   │   └── odi (and bundled files)
38:   └── current -> versions/<version>
39: 
40: ~/.local/bin/
41:   ├── odi -> ../share/agentic-odi/current/odi
42:   ├── odipm
43:   ├── odi-cli
44:   └── agentic-odi
45: 
46: ~/.config/agentic-odi/  # state/preferences
47: ```
48: 
49: Environment variables: `AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR` (override install root),
50: `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_BIN_HOME`. The default backend is `local`
51: (`--backend local`); no MCP server is required.
52: 
53: ## Unsigned binaries
54: 
55: macOS may quarantine downloaded binaries:
56: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ~/.local/bin/odi` (if needed). Windows SmartScreen
57: may show a warning for unsigned binaries; choose "More info → Run anyway" if you
58: trust the release.
59: 
60: ## Release automation
61: 
62: Releases are cut and published by CI with no approval step:
63: 
64: 1. Conventional commits land on `main`; `release-please` opens or updates the
65:    release PR.
66: 2. The `release-please` workflow arms auto-merge on that PR. `main` requires the
67:    `CI green` check (ruleset `main-requires-ci-green`), so the PR merges itself
68:    as soon as CI passes — nobody clicks merge.
69: 3. The merge cuts tag `vX.Y.Z` and the GitHub Release; the tag starts the
70:    `release` and `Tauri Release` workflows, which attach the CLI archives,
71:    `checksums.txt`, the install scripts, and the desktop bundles to it.
72: 4. `e2e-install` runs after `release` succeeds and installs the published binary
73:    on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
74: 
75: **One-time setup (GitHub App).** GitHub holds workflow runs that start from
76: `GITHUB_TOKEN`-authored pushes ("This workflow requires approval from a
77: maintainer") and ignores the tag such a push creates, which is why releases used
78: to need a maintainer. A release-only GitHub App avoids both:
79: 
80: 1. Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App, with
81:    permissions: Contents `Read and write`, Issues `Read and write`, Pull
82:    requests `Read and write` (no webhook).
83: 2. Install the App on this repository.
84: 3. Add repository secrets `RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID` (the App's client ID)
85:    and `RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (a generated private key).
86: 
87: Until those secrets exist, the `release-please` workflow logs a warning and falls
88: back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`: releases still happen, but the release PR needs a
89: maintainer approval and merge, and the tag will not start the asset builds. After
90: adding the secrets, re-run the workflow (`gh workflow run release-please.yml`) or
91: push to `main` so the open release PR is re-driven by the App.
92: 
93: To check the installer without cutting a release, run
94: `bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh` — it serves a simulated release over HTTP and
95: exercises `scripts/install.sh` end to end (CI runs it too).

(End of file - total 95 lines)
</content>

1: # Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend
2: 
3: To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a
4: local LLM backend that:
5: 
6: - Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example,
7:   `/v1/chat/completions`), and
8: - Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**.
9: 
10: A simple fully local option is
11: [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run
12: a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server.
13: 
14: ## 1. Install a local LLM server
15: 
16: Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for
17: platform-specific build notes):
18: 
19: ```bash
20: pip install llama-cpp-python
21: ```
22: 
23: ## 2. Download a small tools-capable model
24: 
25: Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a
26: 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g.
27: `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`.
28: 
29: ## 3. Start the OpenAI-compatible server
30: 
31: Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default
32: used by the Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat:
33: 
34: ```bash
35: python -m llama_cpp.server \
36:   --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \
37:   --model_alias local-tools-model \
38:   --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \
39:   --chat_format openai
40: ```
41: 
42: This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`.
43: 
44: ## 4. Configure the Studio
45: 
46: The Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat read the following environment
47: variables (with sensible defaults):
48: 
49: | Variable | Default |
50: |---|---|
51: | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
52: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` |
53: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
54: | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` |
55: 
56: You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Living Studio's
57: **Settings** panel.
58: 
59: ## 5. Verify tool-calling against the MCP server
60: 
61: - (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable:
62: 
63:   ```bash
64:   curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models
65:   ```
66: 
67:   If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before
68:   debugging the MCP client/server.
69: 
70: - Start the MCP server and Studio (via `python -m client.run` or one of the
71:   [run modes](living-studio.md)).
72: - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for
73:   example: *"Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI
74:   repository."*
75: - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for
76:   example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI
77:   guidance, confirming the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work
78:   together.
79: - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI shows a clear error
80:   banner indicating the configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with
81:   details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps
82:   above to fix your local LLM setup.

(End of file - total 82 lines)
</content>

1: # Superpowers (Pi, OpenCode & Freebuff)
2: 
3: This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a
4: [Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with
5: this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded.
6: 
7: ## Enable with Pi
8: 
9: 1. Install Pi: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh`
10: 2. Trust the project (first time only): `pi config --local --approve`
11: 3. Start Pi: `pi`
12: 
13: The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. Pi clones it and loads:
14: 
15: - **Extension**: `superpowers.ts` — injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at
16:   session startup and after compaction
17: - **Skills**: 12 Superpowers skills (TDD, subagent-driven-development,
18:   systematic-debugging, etc.)
19: 
20: > [!NOTE]
21: > Superpowers is also available for OpenCode via the plugin in `opencode.json`.
22: > The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode
23: > compatibility layer.
24: 
25: ## Freebuff
26: 
27: This project ships [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) for
28: [Freebuff](https://freebuff.com) as repo-local skills plus a session-start
29: bootstrap. No plugin or hook is required:
30: 
31: - **Skills**: `.agents/skills/` contains 15 Superpowers skills. Freebuff
32:   discovers them automatically; load one with the `skill` tool.
33: - **Bootstrap**: `AGENTS.md` injects the `using-superpowers` rules and the
34:   Freebuff tool mapping at session start.
35: - **Mapping**: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md`
36:   maps skill actions to Freebuff tools.
37: 
38: Start Freebuff in the repository and ask "What are your superpowers?" to verify.
39: See [docs/superpowers/freebuff-setup.md](superpowers/freebuff-setup.md) for
40: update and troubleshooting notes.

(End of file - total 40 lines)
</content>

93:         ]:

2:

4:

6:

20: def evaluate_outcome_statement(statement: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
21:     """Return format feedback for a desired-outcome statement."""
22:     text = statement.strip()
23:     lowered = text.lower()
24:     padded = f" {lowered} "
25:     issues: list[str] = []

27:

22: _ENV_VAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")

25: class MissingEnvironmentError(RuntimeError):
26:     """Raised when a connector needs credentials that are not in the environment."""

28:     def __init__(self, names: list[str]) -> None:
29:         self.names = names

31: 
32: 
33: def _expand_env(value: str, environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
34:     return _ENV_VAR_PATTERN.sub(lambda match: environ.get(match.group(1), ""), value)
35: 
36: 
37: def _to_dict(obj: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
38:     if hasattr(obj, "model_dump"):
39:         dumped = obj.model_dump(mode="json")
40:         if isinstance(dumped, dict):
41:             return dumped
42:     return {"repr": repr(obj)}
43: 
44: 
45: def _content_text(obj: Any) -> str:
46:     parts: list[str] = []
47:     content = getattr(obj, "content", None)
48:     if content is None:
49:         text = getattr(obj, "text", None)
50:         return text if isinstance(text, str) else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))
51:     for item in content:
52:         text = getattr(item, "text", None)
53:         if isinstance(text, str):
54:             parts.append(text)
55:     return "\n".join(parts) if parts else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))

58: class MCPClientConnector(Connector):

70:         self.name = name
71:         self.settings = settings
72:         self._server = server
73: 
74:     def transport(self) -> StreamableHttpTransport | FastMCP:
75:         """Build the MCP transport, resolving credentials from the environment."""
76:         if self._server is not None:
77:             return self._server
78:         missing = sorted(name for name in self.settings.env_vars if not os.environ.get(name))
79:         if missing:
80:             raise MissingEnvironmentError(missing)
81:         headers = {
82:             key: _expand_env(value, os.environ) for key, value in self.settings.headers.items()
83:         }
84:         return StreamableHttpTransport(
85:             url=_expand_env(self.settings.url, os.environ),
86:             headers=headers or None,
87:             auth="oauth" if self.settings.auth == "oauth" else None,
88:         )
89: 
90:     def _client(self) -> Client:
91:         return Client(self.transport())

97:                 resources = await client.list_resources()

122:                 resource_dicts = [_to_dict(resource) for resource in resources]

149:                                 raw={"uri": uri, "resource": _to_dict(resource)},
150:                             )
151:                         )
152:                     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
153:                         batch.errors.append(f"Failed to read resource {uri}: {exc}")
154:                 configured_tools = self.settings.tools
155:                 available = {str(getattr(tool, "name", "")) for tool in tools}

11:         self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, check_same_thread=check_same_thread)

16:         """Creates an immutable, append-only event table."""
17:         with self.conn:
18:             self.conn.execute(
19:                 """
20:                 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
21:                     id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
22:                     timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
23:                     event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
24:                     payload TEXT NOT NULL
25:                 )
26:             """
27:             )
28: 
29:     def append(self, event_type: str, payload: dict) -> None:
30:         """Appends a new event to the stream (Immutable write)."""
31:         timestamp = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
32:         payload_json = json.dumps(payload)
33:         with self.conn:
34:             self.conn.execute(
35:                 "INSERT INTO events (timestamp, event_type, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
36:                 (timestamp, event_type, payload_json),
37:             )
38: 
39:     def get_stream(self) -> list[dict]:
40:         """Retrieves the full chronological event stream for AI reasoning."""
41:         cursor = self.conn.cursor()

1: """JSON-backed registry of named connector configurations."""
2: 
3: from __future__ import annotations
4: 
5: import json
6: from pathlib import Path
7: from typing import Any
8: 
9: from connectors.models import ConnectorConfig
10: 
11: 
12: class UnknownConnectorKindError(ValueError):
13:     def __init__(self, kind: str) -> None:
14:         self.kind = kind
15:         super().__init__(f"Unknown connector kind: {kind}")
16: 
17: 
18: class DuplicateConnectorError(ValueError):
19:     def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
20:         self.name = name
21:         super().__init__(f"Connector already exists: {name}")
22: 
23: 
24: class ConnectorNotFoundError(ValueError):
25:     def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
26:         self.name = name
27:         super().__init__(f"Connector not found: {name}")
28: 
29: 
30: def _known_kinds() -> set[str]:
31:     from connectors.factory import known_kinds
32: 
33:     return known_kinds()
34: 
35: 
36: class ConnectorRegistry:
37:     """Persists connector configs to a JSON file."""
38: 
39:     def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
40:         self.path = path
41: 
42:     def add(self, config: ConnectorConfig) -> None:
43:         if config.kind not in _known_kinds():
44:             raise UnknownConnectorKindError(config.kind)
45:         connectors = self._load()
46:         if any(existing.name == config.name for existing in connectors):
47:             raise DuplicateConnectorError(config.name)
48:         connectors.append(config)
49:         self._save(connectors)
50: 
51:     def list_all(self) -> list[ConnectorConfig]:
52:         return self._load()
53: 
54:     def get(self, name: str) -> ConnectorConfig:
55:         for config in self._load():
56:             if config.name == name:
57:                 return config
58:         raise ConnectorNotFoundError(name)
59: 
60:     def _load(self) -> list[ConnectorConfig]:
61:         if not self.path.exists():
62:             return []
63:         with self.path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
64:             payload: dict[str, Any] = json.load(handle)
65:         raw_connectors = payload.get("connectors", [])
66:         return [ConnectorConfig.model_validate(item) for item in raw_connectors]
67: 
68:     def _save(self, connectors: list[ConnectorConfig]) -> None:
69:         self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
70:         payload = {"connectors": [item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in connectors]}
71:         with self.path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
72:             json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2)
73:             handle.write("\n")

15: from local_server.studio.probes import check_llm_health
16: from local_server.studio.schemas import ChatRequest
17: 
18: SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are Steve Jobs and an elite Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) strategist assisting a Product Manager in The Living Studio.
19: Your mission is to eliminate backlog paper-pushing and help the PM think exclusively in human intent, customer friction, and measurable outcomes.
20: Key principles:
21: 1. Always start with the Job-to-be-Done (JTBD): "What is the core functional human job?"
22: 2. Uncover Desired Outcomes using the strict ODI format: [Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]. (e.g. "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments").
23: 3. Opportunity Score = Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0). Scores > 10 represent breakthrough underserved market opportunities.
24: 4. When asked to add or query Jobs, Steps, or Outcomes, ALWAYS invoke the corresponding tools.
25: 5. Embody clarity, focus, and causality. Strip away corporate jargon."""
26: 
27: 
28: def offline_fallback(user_input: str) -> str:
29:     """Intelligent grounded fallback when no LLM backend is reachable."""
30:     lower_inp = user_input.lower()
31:     if "guideline" in lower_inp or "framework" in lower_inp or "stage" in lower_inp:
32:         return (
33:             "### 📖 Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) Process Guidelines\n\n"
34:             "1. **Stage 1: Define Intent (Job-to-be-Done)** — Identify the core functional human goal.\n"
35:             "2. **Stage 2: Capture Desired Outcomes** — Success metrics: `[Direction] + [Unit] + [Object] + [Context]`.\n"
36:             "3. **Stage 3: Opportunity Scoring** — `Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)`. Focus on scores > 10.\n"
37:             "4. **Stage 4: Universal Job Map** — Map the 8 stages: Define ➔ Locate ➔ Prepare ➔ Confirm ➔ Execute ➔ Monitor ➔ Modify ➔ Conclude.\n\n"
38:             "*(Connected in Local Studio Mode. Start your local LLM backend at `http://localhost:8001/v1` for full autonomous completions)*"
39:         )
40:     if "simulate" in lower_inp or "bet" in lower_inp or "impact" in lower_inp:
41:         return (
42:             "### ⚡ WYSIWYG Impact Simulation Result\n\n"
43:             "- **Target Outcome**: O-1 (*Minimize time taken to propagate secrets*)\n"
44:             "- **Proposed Bet**: Automated Secret Sync Daemon\n"
45:             "- **Before**: 45 minutes of manual copy-paste across 400 developer pipelines.\n"
46:             "- **After**: Under 30 seconds ambient zero-touch sync.\n"
47:             "- **Time-to-Value Shift**: **-90% friction reduction**.\n"
48:             "- **Human Impact**: 3,000 hours of developer agony eliminated every month. Build it."
49:         )
50:     if "evidence" in lower_inp or "call" in lower_inp or "quote" in lower_inp:
51:         return (
52:             "### 🔍 Causal Lineage: Real-Time Evidence\n\n"
53:             "- **Signal Source**: Gong Call #104 (Enterprise Team Alpha)\n"
54:             "- **Customer Voice**: *'We lost two hours on deploy day because someone missed a database config key.'*\n"
55:             "- **Telemetry**: 400 microservices impacted weekly; 14% failed build rate attributed to config drift."
56:         )
57:     return (
58:         f'I received your intent: **"{user_input}"**.\n\n'
59:         "In The Living Studio, every idea is evaluated against human outcomes rather than story points. "
60:         "Notice how our highest opportunity outcome (`O-1: Minimize propagation time`) has an **Opportunity Score of 15.3**, "
61:         "signaling severe market underservice. Tap **'Simulate Impact'** on the canvas or type `Simulate Auto-Sync Bet` to test causality."
62:     )

64: 
65: def _sse(event: str, data: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
66:     return f"event: {event}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n"
67: 
68: 
69: def _to_openai_messages(request: ChatRequest) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
70:     messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
71:     for message in request.messages:
72:         messages.append({"role": message.role, "content": message.content})
73:     return messages
74: 
75: 
76: def _openai_tools(mcp_tools: list[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
77:     return [
78:         {
79:             "type": "function",
80:             "function": {
81:                 "name": tool.name,
82:                 "description": tool.description,
83:                 "parameters": tool.input_schema,
84:             },
85:         }
86:         for tool in mcp_tools
87:     ]
88: 
89: 
90: async def stream_chat(request: ChatRequest) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
91:     """Yield SSE frames: status, delta, tool, message, canvas_dirty."""
92:     yield _sse("status", {"phase": "health_check"})
93:     healthy, _message = await check_llm_health(request.base_url, request.api_key, request.model)
94: 
95:     last_user = next((m.content for m in reversed(request.messages) if m.role == "user"), "")
96: 
97:     if not healthy:
98:         reply = offline_fallback(last_user)
99:         yield _sse("delta", {"text": reply})
100:         yield _sse("message", {"content": reply})
101:         return
102: 
103:     yield _sse("status", {"phase": "mcp_tools"})
104:     llm_client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=request.base_url, api_key=request.api_key, timeout=15.0)
105: 
106:     async with McpClient(request.mcp_url) as mcp_client:
107:         mcp_tools = await mcp_client.list_tools()
108:         openai_tools = _openai_tools(mcp_tools)
109:         messages: list[Any] = _to_openai_messages(request)
110: 
111:         yield _sse("status", {"phase": "model"})
112:         stream: Any = await llm_client.chat.completions.create(  # type: ignore[call-overload]
113:             model=request.model,
114:             messages=messages,
115:             tools=openai_tools if openai_tools else None,
116:             tool_choice="auto" if openai_tools else None,
117:             stream=True,
118:         )
119: 
120:         buffered_text: list[str] = []
121:         tool_calls: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}
122: 
123:         async for chunk in stream:
124:             delta = chunk.choices[0].delta
125:             if delta.content:
126:                 buffered_text.append(delta.content)
127:             for tool_call in delta.tool_calls or []:
128:                 entry = tool_calls.setdefault(
129:                     tool_call.index, {"id": "", "name": "", "arguments": ""}
130:                 )
131:                 if tool_call.id:
132:                     entry["id"] = tool_call.id
133:                 if tool_call.function is not None:
134:                     if tool_call.function.name:
135:                         entry["name"] = tool_call.function.name
136:                     if tool_call.function.arguments:
137:                         entry["arguments"] += tool_call.function.arguments
138: 
139:         if not tool_calls:
140:             content = "".join(buffered_text)
141:             if content:
142:                 yield _sse("delta", {"text": content})
143:             yield _sse("message", {"content": content})
144:             return
145: 
146:         messages.append(
147:             {
148:                 "role": "assistant",
149:                 "content": None,
150:                 "tool_calls": [
151:                     {
152:                         "id": entry["id"],
153:                         "type": "function",
154:                         "function": {
155:                             "name": entry["name"],
156:                             "arguments": entry["arguments"] or "{}",
157:                         },
158:                     }
159:                     for entry in tool_calls.values()
160:                 ],
161:             }
162:         )
163: 
164:         for entry in tool_calls.values():
165:             name = entry["name"]
166:             yield _sse("tool", {"name": name, "status": "start"})
167:             try:
168:                 arguments = json.loads(entry["arguments"] or "{}")
169:             except json.JSONDecodeError:
170:                 arguments = {}
171: 
172:             try:
173:                 result = await mcp_client.call_tool(name, arguments)
174:                 result_str = str(result)
175:                 yield _sse("tool", {"name": name, "status": "ok", "preview": result_str[:280]})
176:             except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
177:                 result_str = f"Error calling {name}: {exc}"
178:                 yield _sse("tool", {"name": name, "status": "error", "preview": result_str})
179: 
180:             messages.append(
181:                 {
182:                     "role": "tool",
183:                     "tool_call_id": entry["id"],
184:                     "name": name,
185:                     "content": result_str,
186:                 }
187:             )
188: 
189:         yield _sse("canvas_dirty", {"value": True})
190: 
191:         final_stream: Any = await llm_client.chat.completions.create(
192:             model=request.model,
193:             messages=messages,
194:             stream=True,
195:         )
196:         final_parts: list[str] = []
197:         async for chunk in final_stream:
198:             delta = chunk.choices[0].delta
199:             if delta.content:
200:                 final_parts.append(delta.content)
201:                 yield _sse("delta", {"text": delta.content})
202: 
203:         yield _sse("message", {"content": "".join(final_parts)})

1: # Superpowers for Freebuff
2: 
3: Freebuff uses the same [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) methodology as the OpenCode and Pi integrations, delivered through the two surfaces Freebuff loads automatically:
4: 
5: 1. **Skills** — `.agents/skills/` contains the 15 Superpowers skills. Freebuff scans `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`, validates each frontmatter block, and lists every skill's name and description in the system prompt. The `skill` tool loads one by name.
6: 2. **Bootstrap** — `AGENTS.md` at the repository root carries the `using-superpowers` bootstrap, the Freebuff tool mapping, and a pointer to the project guardrails. Freebuff loads project `AGENTS.md` at session start, so the methodology is active without a plugin or hook. The section is explicitly scoped to Freebuff so OpenCode and Pi keep using their own integrations.
7: 3. **Reference mapping** — `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md` is the detailed action-to-tool translation. `AGENTS.md` inlines the same mapping so it is present even before a skill is loaded.
8: 
9: ## Layout
10: 
11: ```text
12: AGENTS.md                                        # session-start bootstrap + Freebuff mapping
13: .agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md                  # 15 vendored Superpowers skills
14: .agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/
15:   freebuff-tools.md                              # detailed Freebuff tool mapping
16: skills-lock.json                                 # source + hash for `npx skills update`
17: ```
18: 
19: ## First run
20: 
21: Freebuff may ask whether to trust a repository's `.agents` directory the first time it sees one. Approve it interactively, or pass `--trust-agents` (intended for CI) when starting Freebuff.
22: 
23: ## Verify
24: 
25: Start a fresh Freebuff session in this repository and ask:
26: 
27: ```text
28: What are your superpowers?
29: ```
30: 
31: The agent should know it has Superpowers and list the installed skills. The real acceptance check is:
32: 
33: ```text
34: Let's make a react todo list
35: ```
36: 
37: `brainstorming` must trigger before any code is written.
38: 
39: ## Updating
40: 
41: The skill tree is committed, so a fresh clone needs no install step. To pull the latest Superpowers skills:
42: 
43: ```bash
44: npx skills update -y
45: ```
46: 
47: To reinstall from upstream:
48: 
49: ```bash
50: npx skills add obra/superpowers --agent universal --skill '*' --copy -y
51: ```
52: 
53: The `universal` target installs to `.agents/skills/`, which is the directory Freebuff scans. After an update, confirm `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md` still exists; the `AGENTS.md` bootstrap is independent of the skill tree and survives skill updates.
54: 
55: ## Freebuff limitations
56: 
57: - **No subagent tool.** Use `executing-plans` instead of `subagent-driven-development`, and run independent tasks sequentially instead of `dispatching-parallel-agents`.
58: - **No plan mode.** Designs and plans are written to `docs/superpowers/specs/` and `docs/superpowers/plans/` with `write_file`.
59: - **No session hooks.** `AGENTS.md` is the session-start surface; there is no plugin to install and no per-session opt-in.
60: - **Compaction.** `write_todos` is a live view. Keep the durable ledger from `executing-plans` under `.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/progress.md`.
